decisions.reason: The candidate already records the background and header-logo shell from message 56. The landing-page background treatment is specifically stated for AWS Cognito authentication pages and does not necessarily apply to every informational page.
The Cognito branding change does not alter the policy destinations or their footer access point; those requirements arise from a separate clause in the same message.

The informational-page shell is already represented by REQ_INFORMATIONAL_PAGE_SHELL. The Cognito-specific landing-page background treatment does not change the wizard's internal typography, layout, controls, or unresolved accent choice.
Reusing the landing-page background on Cognito pages does not modify the landing page's own visual direction.
The Cognito sign-in branding decision does not change the landing page's copy plan, section order, How It Works sequence, or sequence visual.
The source decision does not change whether the landing page requires a sign-up button.
The source specifies Cognito visual branding but makes no change to landing-page responsive behavior.
A header logo on the sign-in page does not imply enabling or changing the landing page's header navigation menu.

Message 56 already has a separate footer MODIFY for its footer-specific clauses. The Cognito branding change does not necessitate another footer update, and footer inclusion on the informational pages is stated only as a possibility.
Using the landing-page background for Cognito is consistent with the existing landing-page theme reference and does not change the shared website theme state.
The Cognito background and header-logo treatment does not affect hero-text emphasis on the landing page.
The sign-in branding decision does not modify the landing page's plain HTML and Tailwind CSS build stack.
